copy.blurb:
A +13.8pp gap on the Tunisia side. Sweden v Tunisia in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Tunisia stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

Elo numbers going in: Sweden 1660, Tunisia 1650. That's a 10-point lead for Sweden — closer than a casual reader of the market price might assume. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Sweden to win at 36%, the draw at 29%, and Tunisia to win at 34%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Sweden to win at 50%, the draw at 28%, and Tunisia to win at 20%. On the Tunisia side specifically the market reads 20%, which prices out at American odds of +388. Compared against the model's 34%, that's the +13.8pp gap the Pick rests on.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Tunisia the lower bound is 29%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +8.7pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The point is selection, not a blanket call. Most matches the model and the market agree on. This is one of the ones where they don't, and the gap is on the Tunisia side specifically.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 20 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.

copy.summary: A +13.8pp gap across model and market on the Tunisia side. Our Elo prior, after host and altitude adjustments, rates Tunisia at 34%; Polymarket sits at 20%.
